name: Progress Monitoring and Fidelity
title: Progress Monitoring and Fidelity
answer: Progress monitoring and fidelity means tracking whether a student is moving toward their goals and checking whether the planned interventions are actually being delivered. AI tools in spreadsheets and special education data systems can chart and summarize the data, which saves time and makes patterns easier to see. It matters because teams can see whether services are happening, but the data does not explain why a student is or is not progressing.

sections.body: Progress monitoring is the practice of collecting data, often weekly, to see whether a student is moving toward their goals. Teachers look for trends in that data rather than relying on a single point. AI tools in spreadsheets and special education data systems can turn the data into charts and short summaries. This reduces the time spent on manual charting and can make patterns easier to notice. The problem it solves is that teams need a clear view of both student progress and whether interventions are being delivered as planned.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or classroom, teachers collect progress data, often weekly, and review it for trends. AI tools in spreadsheets and special education data systems can produce charts and short summaries from that data. Teams then use those summaries to monitor progress and to check fidelity, which means whether interventions were delivered as planned. The text does not give separate grade bands for this practice. The team interprets the data, not the tool, so the charts and summaries are starting points for discussion.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels the evidence as a small review. It found that AI tools were associated with better monitoring of whether interventions were delivered as planned, a quality called fidelity (Mosher, 2026). Links to student outcomes were indirect, since the review included only five studies. The finding suggests AI can help teams see whether services are actually happening. It does not yet show that students learn more as a result.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The team interprets the data, not the tool. A summary might say a student is not making progress, but the reasons could range from an ineffective intervention to missed sessions to a hard stretch at home. Only people who know the student can sort out which reason applies. The data starts the conversation, and the team finishes it. Decisions about what the data means and what to do next stay with the people who know the student.
